findings.title: Grafana list items are rendered without a React key
findings.body: In FilterViewResults, rules.map destructures a key and passes it to DataSourceRuleLoader and UnknownRuleListItem, but for origin === 'grafana' it returns GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key}. In an infinite-scroll list this can cause React reconciliation problems and duplicate/incorrect DOM reuse when new pages are appended.

findings.title: Typo adds an extra '}' to Grafana rule keys
findings.body: getGrafanaRuleKey returns `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}}`, which appends an unintended trailing curly brace to every Grafana rule key. The key may still be unique, but this is a typo that can make keys harder to debug and suggests the template literal was not intended to end with `}}`.

findings.title: Silence menu item can be shown but the silence drawer never opens in the Prometheus-only list
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now computes silence support from Grafana Prometheus rule abilities, so in the new list view where only promRule is supplied the 'Silence notifications' menu item can be rendered. However RuleActionsButtons only mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, and rule is undefined in this flow. Clicking Silence therefore sets local state but renders no drawer, making the action silently do nothing.

findings.title: Delete action is hidden for Prometheus-only Grafana rules even when allowed
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu computes canDelete from both ruler abilities and Grafana Prometheus abilities, but the Delete menu item is only rendered when rulerRule is truthy. In the new alert list flow GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons supplies only promRule, so users with delete permission will not see Delete even though canDelete can be true and the delete handler in RuleActionsButtons can operate using the rule identifier alone.

findings.title: Pause action is not rendered for Prometheus-only Grafana rules although pause ability is computed
findings.body: canPause can become true from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, but MenuItemPauseRule is only rendered when a rulerRule is present. Since the new list view removes ruler data and passes only promRule, pause becomes unavailable even though the new Grafana Prometheus ability hook reports it as supported/allowed. If pause truly requires ruler data, the ability should not be reported as supported; otherwise the pause menu item needs a Prometheus-rule-compatible implementation.

findings.title: Federated ruler rules are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false, while the previous useAllAlertRuleAbilities implementation used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). The deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to this hook, so existing callers that pass CombinedRule lose the federated check. Federated Mimir rule groups may now be considered editable/deletable/pausable/duplicable, exposing actions that should be unsupported and potentially allowing users to attempt mutations they should not be allowed to perform.

findings.title: Menu test asserts Silence item exists but never exercises the action
findings.body: The test clicks More and asserts that the Silence menu item is present, but it does not click the item or verify that a silence drawer opens. Because the new Prometheus-only list item has no ruler rule, the current implementation renders the Silence menu item but does not mount the corresponding drawer, so this test can pass while the user-visible action is broken.
